app.name: Habit Tracker
app.oneLiner: A daily habit tracker with streaks, daily check-in, and reminders.
app.problem: People who want to build a habit forget to do it on day two. The reminder fires, they snooze, and the streak they were excited about the day before is gone before week one ends. They need a single screen that says what to do today, what they did yesterday, and what is at risk if they skip today — and they need it to be the first thing they see.
app.targetUsers: Adults forming one to three new habits at a time, comfortable with a phone, not comfortable with a journal.
nonGoals: Social features. A streak that belongs to your friend group is a different product.
Analytics dashboards beyond a streak counter and a weekly completion ring.
Habit libraries. The user names their own habits, period.

in: Today's habits list, with check-off and current streak per row
Stats tab with weekly completion ring and per-habit streak history
Local notifications: one per habit, daily at the user's chosen time
out: Premium tier or paywall (free for MVP)

decisions.question: Does a habit need an account, or does it live on the device?
decisions.answer: On the device. No auth in the MVP.

decisions.question: Does a missed day break the streak, or is there a grace day?
decisions.answer: A missed day breaks it. No grace day.

decisions.question: Can a habit repeat more than once a day?
decisions.answer: No — one check-in per habit per day.
decisions.why: Multiple check-ins turns the ring into a counter and the streak into an average; that is a different app

decisions.question: Do reminders fire locally or from a server?
decisions.why: A server-side reminder needs accounts and a scheduler, and auth is already out of the MVP

navigation.ascii:
Home shell
  ├─ /habits           Today (tab 1)
  ├─ /habits/new       New habit (pushed)
  ├─ /habits/:id       Habit detail (pushed from row)
  ├─ /habits/:id/edit  Edit habit (pushed from detail)
  ├─ /stats            Stats (tab 2)
  └─ /settings         Settings (tab 3)

tokens: Habit ring colour reuses palette.action for completed streaks
Streak numbers use typography.headlineSmall for at-a-glance readability
Day cells in stats use spacing.half-step

routes.name: Today
routes.purpose: one hero (today's date + ring), then a bento of the three habits due

lookAndFeel.header: DSLargeAppBar with the date as title, the count as subtitle
lookAndFeel.motion: Tap-to-check fires a 200ms ring-fill on the row, no other animation
lookAndFeel.darkMode: Ring colour stays the same; tile surfaces use the surface ladder, not pure white

accessibility: Each row's checkbox announces habit name + streak ('Read 10 pages, 5 day streak')
The hero's ring is decorative and aria-hidden; the count is read from the subtitle
designSystemRules: Every checkbox uses DSTapTarget — VoiceOver users get the same hit area as everyone else
No inline Theme.of(context).primary — all colours come from tokens
verification: Text scale 2.0: every row's streak chip stays inside its tap target
Narrow width (390pt): the bento rows reflow to a single column without clipping
nonGoals: Streak history on the home screen — that lives in the Stats tab

endpoints.purpose: list today's habits with completion state

states.loading: Six skeleton rows in the bento; the ring is half-painted until the count arrives.
states.empty: No habits yet. The hero says 'Add your first habit'. One button: New habit.
states.error: Habits could not be loaded. Pull to refresh.
states.success: Today's list renders, the ring fills as rows check off.

components.purpose: Carried forward from the legacy control/why/rejected triple. See the per-feature plan for the role of this kit on this route.
components.why: It carries the date+count subtitle and pushes back under scroll, which makes the bento the content rather than a header chrome strip
rejected: a custom AppBar with a CircularProgressIndicator drawn in it

components.purpose: Carried forward from the legacy control/why/rejected triple. See the per-feature plan for the role of this kit on this route.
components.why: Row is the only pattern that supports a leading checkbox and trailing streak chip without hand-rolling layout
rejected: Card with a Row of widgets, which ui-lint will reject anyway

gestures.behavior: marks the habit complete for today
gestures.transition: checkmark scales in, streak count ticks up

journeys.name: Check in and see the streak grow

routes.name: All habits
routes.purpose: every habit the user has, filterable by status

lookAndFeel.header: Plain DSAppBar — no large variant, this is a pushed route so the back chevron matters
lookAndFeel.motion: Swipe-archive animates a 240ms slide-out; no other motion
lookAndFeel.darkMode: Filter chip selected state uses surface-2; non-selected uses surface-1

accessibility: Each row announces habit name + current streak + filter status
Swipe-to-archive has a confirm step so a misfire is recoverable
designSystemRules: Every control from the kit; no inline Theme.of(context) colours
verification: Text scale 2.0: filter chips do not overlap the search field
Pull-to-refresh works on every filter state

integration.note: 'See all' link in the bento's footer

states.loading: Six skeleton rows, same height as a real one.
states.empty: No habits yet. 'Add your first habit' with a primary action.
states.zeroResults: No habits match that filter or search. Clear filters.
states.success: The list renders; pull-to-refresh updates it.

components.purpose: Carried forward from the legacy control/why/rejected triple. See the per-feature plan for the role of this kit on this route.
components.why: Archive is a common destructive action and a swipe is the gesture users already have for it on iOS
rejected: a trailing icon button on every row, which crowds the row

components.purpose: Carried forward from the legacy control/why/rejected triple. See the per-feature plan for the role of this kit on this route.
components.why: The swipe's tappable twin — a swipe with no twin is invisible to a reader using VoiceOver

components.purpose: Carried forward from the legacy control/why/rejected triple. See the per-feature plan for the role of this kit on this route.
components.why: Search in place, not a separate search route
rejected: a search icon that pushes a full-screen search route

gestures.behavior: archives the habit, with undo in a snack bar

journeys.name: Find a habit and open it

routes.name: Habit detail
routes.purpose: one habit, with its streak history and edit access
routes.subtitle: 12-day streak

lookAndFeel.header: DSLargeAppBar; subtitle is the streak count; overflow menu holds Pause / Archive
lookAndFeel.motion: Day cells highlight on tap with a 150ms fade, no other motion
lookAndFeel.darkMode: Section background uses surface-1; the today cell uses action.tint at 10% alpha

accessibility: Day cells are tappable and announce the date + completion state
Edit button has the same hit area as the screen's primary tap targets
designSystemRules: No inline Theme.of(context).primary — every colour from tokens
verification: Long content (180-day history) still has the pinned bar above the safe area
nonGoals: Graphing the streak. Counts and a list are enough.

endpoints.purpose: fetch one habit with its history

states.loading: The title renders from the row that opened it; the body is bones.
states.empty: An archived habit reads 'Archived on <date>' and offers Unarchive.
states.error: This habit could not be opened. Back to list.
states.success: Detail renders and the pinned bar stays put while it scrolls.

components.purpose: Carried forward from the legacy control/why/rejected triple. See the per-feature plan for the role of this kit on this route.
components.why: Edit must not scroll away on a long history; the pinned bar is what makes Detail the archetype it is
rejected: a FAB, which covers the last row of the history

components.purpose: Carried forward from the legacy control/why/rejected triple. See the per-feature plan for the role of this kit on this route.
components.why: Pause and Archive are destructive — they go in the overflow, not in a row of three buttons
rejected: two more buttons next to Edit

gestures.behavior: pops back to the list (iOS edge-swipe)

routes.name: Edit habit
routes.purpose: create or edit a habit's name, time, and reminder

lookAndFeel.header: DSAppBar with title 'New habit' or 'Edit habit', cancel on the left
lookAndFeel.motion: Field focus animates the helper label up; nothing else moves
lookAndFeel.darkMode: Field background uses surface-2; helper uses textTheme.bodySmall

accessibility: Each field's label is read with the field, not above it
Validation errors replace the helper, not the label
designSystemRules: Field spacing uses spacing.field, not arbitrary gaps
verification: Keyboard avoidance: the pinned bar stays above the keyboard, the focused field stays visible
nonGoals: Inline habit icon picker. Ship a placeholder for the MVP.

states.loading: Fields render disabled until the habit arrives.
states.empty: A new habit opens with the name field focused.
states.error: This habit could not be saved. Nothing was lost.
states.success: Save returns to the detail page with the new values on it.

components.purpose: Carried forward from the legacy control/why/rejected triple. See the per-feature plan for the role of this kit on this route.
components.why: It owns the label-above / helper-below contract — when validation fires, the layout does not jump

components.purpose: Carried forward from the legacy control/why/rejected triple. See the per-feature plan for the role of this kit on this route.
components.why: Save is full-width and above the safe area, the Form archetype's only legal primary placement
rejected: a floating Save button, which is the desktop pattern

routes.name: Stats
routes.purpose: weekly completion ring per habit and a settings-style scroll list

lookAndFeel.motion: Ring fills on scroll-into-view, 300ms once, never again
lookAndFeel.darkMode: Eyebrow uses textTheme.labelSmall; rows use surface-1

accessibility: Each ratio is also written as text ('5 of 7'), so a screen reader does not need to parse the ring
designSystemRules: Ring size follows DesignSpec.progressSize.large; no hand-coded dimensions
verification: Empty state: no habits yet, a 'Stats will appear once you start a habit' message
nonGoals: Charts beyond per-habit ratios. No line graphs, no heatmaps.

endpoints.purpose: completion counts per habit for the last 7 days

states.empty: Stats will appear once you start a habit.
states.error: Stats could not be loaded. Pull to refresh.

components.purpose: Carried forward from the legacy control/why/rejected triple. See the per-feature plan for the role of this kit on this route.
components.why: Settings-style grouped inset rows. Stats is a list of facts, not a hero page
rejected: a Card per habit, which is the dashboard pattern

components.purpose: Carried forward from the legacy control/why/rejected triple. See the per-feature plan for the role of this kit on this route.
components.why: The completion ratio is the dominant fact; a ring encodes ratio without a legend
rejected: a progress bar, which encodes completion but not ratio visually

lookAndFeel.header: DSAppBar with 'Settings' title, plain (no large variant)
lookAndFeel.motion: No animation; settings is a read-mostly list
lookAndFeel.darkMode: Grouped rows use surface-1, eyebrows use textTheme.labelSmall

accessibility: Each row's right value is also the focusable tap target, not just the chevron
designSystemRules: Destructive actions would live in their own bottom group (none in MVP)
verification: Text scale 2.0: every row's right value stays inside its cell
nonGoals: Account / sign-in — auth is deferred to post-MVP

states.empty: Not applicable — settings has at least three rows.
states.error: Settings could not be loaded. Try again.
states.success: Settings render and every tap target is reachable.

components.purpose: Carried forward from the legacy control/why/rejected triple. See the per-feature plan for the role of this kit on this route.
components.why: Grouped inset rows by what the user is changing, not by which service owns it
rejected: a ListView of ListTiles, which is what ui-lint forbids
